text:
maria.k: hi all — brand new hire here, trying to clone our repo from WSL2 (Ubuntu) but it fails with timeout to git.internal.redwood.dev. Windows native git works. We're on Okta AnyConnect with split-tunnel. any tips?
jonathan: welcome! this is a known WSL2 split-tunnel quirk. quick debug: from WSL run `ip route` and `curl -v --resolve git.internal.redwood.dev:443:10.40.12.5 https://git.internal.redwood.dev/` to see where traffic goes.
maria.k: ok running that now: `ip route` shows default via 172.24.112.1 dev eth0, no 10.40 route. curl just hangs. Windows `ipconfig` shows VPN adapter with route to 10.40.0.0/16.
jonathan: yep — windows has the VPN routes but WSL2 VM does not. Two common workarounds: (A) add a route inside WSL pointing at the Windows host gateway, (B) use the bastion as a jump host for git/ssh. If you need native tooling inside WSL, route is easiest.
maria.k: how to add route so it survives restarts? dont want to re-add every reboot.
leo: simplest: create a small script in your WSL home and call it from `~/.profile`. example:
```
# ~/bin/wsl-vpn-route.sh
#!/bin/sh
# adjust NETWORK and GW to match your VPN/net
sudo ip route add 10.40.0.0/16 via 172.24.112.1 dev eth0 || true
```
then `chmod +x ~/bin/wsl-vpn-route.sh` and add `~/bin/wsl-vpn-route.sh` to `~/.profile`. Note: script will prompt for sudo the first time each session.
maria.k: i dont love storing password prompts. any way to avoid sudo prompt?
jonathan: you can allow that specific ip route command in sudoers without a password (infra policy permitting). file on Windows-managed laptops may be restricted; if you need that, open a ticket and infra can push a small policy.
maria.k: ok that makes sense. i tried manual `sudo ip route add 10.40.0.0/16 via 172.24.112.1` and git clone started working. thanks!
infra-bot: FYI docs: https://wiki.redwood.internal/vpn/wsl2-split-tunnel. If you'd prefer not to touch routing, you can set up git over SSH via the bastion: `ssh -J ec2-bastion git@git.internal.redwood.dev`.
leo: one gotcha: if you disconnect and reconnect VPN, WSL's virtual NIC can change; if route stops working, `wsl --shutdown` from PowerShell then reopen WSL and run the route script.
maria.k: saved this to my onboarding notes and pinged people in #devex. Appreciate the quick help! :party_popper:
